plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the late-winter garden with rose-like blooms. The flowers are layered, satiny and slightly waxy, and they stand out against dark, polished leaves. Single, semi-double and fully double forms all appear in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter into early spring, with many cultivars peaking around February
plants.location: Southeastern United States, especially the Carolinas, where mild winters suit it
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Small, nodding white bells push up through cold soil and sometimes through snow. Each flower has three long outer petals around a shorter inner cup marked with a green notch. Snowdrops often form drifts under bare trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January through March, typically peaking in February in cool temperate regions
plants.location: Temperate Europe, and gardens in cool regions of North America such as the Chicago area
plants.funFact: Snowdrop bulbs make a natural compound, galantamine, that has been developed into a medicine used for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: This small tree flowers on bare branches before its leaves appear. The blossoms are spicily fragrant and are borne singly or in pairs. They cover the branches in soft pink and white, a welcome sign that winter is ending.
plants.bloomingSeason: February to March in colder temperate gardens, and earlier in mild-winter climates
plants.location: Native to southern China. Widely grown in temperate gardens across East Asia and North America, for example in the St. Louis region.
plants.funFact: Ume is prized in East Asia for both its blossoms and its sour fruit, which is pickled or steeped into plum wine.
